title: Runlog mapping (schema version 1)

kind.description: What this document is. A pack says nothing, a setup says `setup`, this says `mapping`.

schemaVersion.description: The format's major version, as a pack carries one.

version.description: Semantic version. A mapping that changes what it does changes this.

title.description: What it is called, on a card and in a chooser.

author.description: Who wrote it. A mapping travels on its own, so this is the only credit it carries.

description.description: What playing under it is like, in a line or two.

tool.description: The tool this is for, by the name that tool calls itself when it attaches.

packs.description: Packs the author wrote this against, so a chooser can offer the likely ones first. Not a restriction: a mapping fires on any pack carrying the marks it names.

items.description: Globally unique pack identifier in reverse-DNS form, e.g. com.example.my-game. Use a domain you control so two packs never collide in a player's library.

mark.description: The mark this fires on. Any pack that declares it and carries it will set this off.

label.description: What to call this rule in a list, where the mark alone is not enough.

for.description: Seconds it lasts. Absent and without `until`, it does not come off.

until.description: Lasts until the unit it landed in closes.

to.description: One seat's name, or absent for everybody at the table.

op.description: The operation, in the tool's own words: `speffect.apply`, `runes.give`. A tool refuses by name anything its build does not have.

args.description: What the operation takes. Its shape is the tool's business, not this format's.

ops.description: What to do when it fires, in order.

rules.description: The rules, in order. Every one that matches fires.

id.description: An SPDX identifier where there is one, else whatever name the terms go by.

redistributable.description: Whether somebody may pass this on.

description: What a tool attached to the game should do about what the dice said, bound to the marks a pack declares rather than to one pack's entries, so one mapping fits every pack for the same game.
